title: 复现账号到发布和后台执行的关键旅程

environment.profile: ORCHARA_PROFILE=dev-stub (no vendor credentials, endpoints or GPU)
environment.network: loopback only; real HTTP (external) + real mTLS (internal)

journeys.title: 账号启动：migrate → bootstrap → 邀请 → 激活 → 登录
entry_commands: cmd/admin migrate (real compiled binary, stack fixture)
cmd/admin bootstrap --login admin --display-name 'Platform Admin' (real binary, password on stdin)
cmd/admin bootstrap --login admin2 (boundary replay of the same real binary)
entry_http: POST /api/v1/admin/users (anonymous; creator; duplicate login; missing CSRF; bad role)
POST /api/v1/auth/activate (unknown token; weak password; expired token; reused token)
truth_sources: platform.principals / platform.users / platform.role_bindings / platform.audit_events (bootstrap-once + invitation facts)
assertions: real cmd/admin migrate applied a continuous migration chain (52 rows, head 0052=0052_handoff_scope_bounds.sql)
real cmd/admin bootstrap created exactly one admin principal (user row, admin role, bootstrap audit event, argon2id hash); the password never appears in the hash
a second real `cmd/admin bootstrap` exits non-zero with 'already exists' and creates no second principal/user
POST /auth/login returns a real session cookie + CSRF; GET /auth/me returns the admin identity and the cookie/CSRF are stored only as SHA-256 in platform.sessions
POST /admin/users returns a one-time activation token; PostgreSQL holds only its SHA-256, the user keeps the !pending-activation sentinel and the creator role + user.invited audit event are real rows
anonymous POST /admin/users is 401 unauthenticated; a non-admin creator gets 403 forbidden and no user row is created
duplicate invite is 409 login_taken; a missing CSRF header is 403 csrf_invalid; an unknown role is 422 validation_failed; all three create no user row
an unknown activation token is 409 activation_invalid
a weak password is 422 validation_failed and does not consume the token (sentinel and consumed_at unchanged); the same token then activates with a valid password
an invitation whose server-side deadline has passed is 409 activation_expired and stays unconsumed (clock-only SQL write, no fabricated business state)
POST /auth/activate succeeds exactly once: argon2id hash stored, must_change_password cleared, token consumed; reusing the old token is 409 activation_consumed
POST /auth/login with the activated password returns the creator session; GET /auth/me returns its principal/roles/CSRF
a wrong password is 401 invalid_credentials and creates no session row
every principal has a user row (5 principals / 5 users); the session/role/token tables hold only real rows written by the exercised endpoints
notes: expiry boundary: only the token's server-side expires_at was moved into the past (clock-only write); the token and user were created by the real invite API
f01's known collection conflict is avoided: this suite imports only tests/support helpers (never tests/f01/conftest.py), so no separate pytest process is needed for this account evidence

journeys.title: 模型登记 → validate → 评测读取 → 通过（dev-stub）
entry_commands: cmd/maintenance run --kinds artifact_finalize (real compiled binary beside it, required because the validation handler waits for its own sealed report)
entry_http: POST /api/v1/models {provider:stub, model_id:stub-model-1, endpoint_ref, secret_ref, config, data_destination} (admin + CSRF)
POST /api/v1/models + /validate for an incompatible stub model and for an undeployed real provider (failure boundaries)
truth_sources: object directory: sealed compatibility document + sealed dataset bytes (sha256)
cmd/maintenance stdout JSON reports + exit code
assertions: POST /models by the admin returns 201 {id, state:pending}; PostgreSQL holds a real pending model profile version with a 64-hex manifest and the stub destination
a non-admin creator gets 403 forbidden for POST /models and POST /models/{id}/validate, and no background job is created
validate without Idempotency-Key is 400 idempotency_key_required (located on the header) and creates no background job

POST /models/{id}/validate returns 202 EvaluationJob(kind=model, state=queued); the same Idempotency-Key replays the identical body and creates exactly one evaluation + one model_validate background job
the real `cmd/maintenance run --once --kinds model_validate` (beside a real artifact_finalize worker) claims and completes the job with result=succeeded
GET /evaluations/{id} is 200 state=succeeded with the report id; GET /evaluation-reports/{id} is 200 status=passed; GET /models/{id} reports validation_state=passed and the same report id

independent truth agrees: model row passed + report bound; evaluation row succeeded; report row passed; the sealed dataset's sha256 equals the report's dataset_sha256; the sealed compatibility document says provider=stub, stub=true, compatible=true; the model-call ledger holds exactly one succeeded row bound to the report artifact
a non-admin creator sees the passed model in GET /models (validation controls visibility)
an incompatible stub model completes the job but records a failed report and a failed model; the failed model is invisible to non-admin listModels (only the passed one stays)
a model naming an undeployed real provider fails validation with the located terminal code provider_not_configured, the evaluation row fails, and no report row is written
notes: stub/real split: the registry, validation job, maintenance handler, sealed report and contract reads are real product code; the compatibility verdict is produced by the dev-stub adapter (document.provider=stub, document.stub=true) and is reported as stub

variants.evidence: this environment has ORCHARA_PROFILE=dev-stub only: no vendor endpoint, credential or GPU exists, so no real model's compatibility/quality was exercised or claimed

journeys.title: 草稿 → validate → 真实评测 → 审核 → 不可变发布版本
entry_commands: cmd/maintenance run --once (real full-kind pools: application_evaluate + artifact_finalize; started by T068's runner helper)
cmd/supervisor exec --once (real compiled supervisor per evaluation case; WSL2/runsc sandbox)
entry_http: POST /api/v1/reviews/{id}/decision (non-admin; mismatched hash; admin approve; replay)
POST /api/v1/conversations + POST /api/v1/requests (chat-text gap probe, explicit application_version_id) + GET /api/v1/runs/{id} + node-results
truth_sources: platform.manifest_artifacts + object directory sealed manifest bytes (sha256)
cmd/maintenance + cmd/supervisor stdout JSON reports and exit codes
assertions: POST /applications/{id}/validate returns {valid:true, errors:[]} and a 64-hex X-Manifest-SHA256; the compiler's sealed manifest artifact has the same hash and its object bytes hash back to it
validate of a draft depending on a pending model returns valid:false with the located dependency_not_ready error, no X-Manifest-SHA256 header, no manifest artifact and no version
the real five-category evaluation (maintenance pools + one real `cmd/supervisor exec --once` per case in WSL2/runsc) ends in a passed sealed report
GET /evaluations/{id} is 200 state=succeeded with the report id and GET /evaluation-reports/{id} is 200 status=passed (both owner-readable contract reads)
the evaluated snapshot's manifest hash equals the validated manifest hash; the sealed report covers five genuine categories (succeeded, node_input_invalid x2, row_limit_exceeded, sandbox_unavailable)
POST /applications/{id}/submit returns 202 {id, state:submitted}; the review row freezes the same manifest hash and a snapshot whose author_cases cover all five categories

submission boundaries: another creator gets 404 resource_not_found (no review created), a wrong expected manifest hash is 409 manifest_mismatch, a missing Idempotency-Key is 400 idempotency_key_required

review decision boundaries: a non-admin creator is 403 forbidden, a mismatched manifest hash is 409 manifest_mismatch with the reviewed hash in details; the admin approval is 200 {state:approved, version_id} and creates exactly one version

independent truth: exactly one application_versions row (version_no 1) bound to the approved review and the validated manifest artifact; the sealed manifest bytes hash to the evaluated manifest; the active pointer, one catalog_index outbox row and the publication.approved audit event are real rows; GET /versions and GET /applications agree

immutability: a second decision is 409 review_conflict(state=approved), identical re-submission returns the same approved review (no second review/version), and a real draft edit + revalidate yields a different manifest hash while the published version row and sealed bytes stay byte-identical and the active pointer does not move
notes: POST /applications/{id}/publication-preview is a real product route but is NOT one of the 106 OpenAPI operations (non-contract route); it is only a pre-submit read here
known product gap recorded separately (status blocked): chat text as a published Run input fails node_input_invalid; see reports/f12/T100-journeys.md §已知产品缺口

journeys.title: worker 终结双证据：submitWorkerResult + confirmAttemptExit（两种顺序）
entry_commands: cmd/maintenance run --once --kinds artifact_finalize (real binary: upload completion -> sealed output artifact)
cmd/supervisor exec --once (real product executor variant; WSL2/runsc)
entry_http: POST /internal/v1/runs/{id}/artifact-uploads + signed PUT + complete + POST /internal/v1/runs/{id}/artifacts (real output registration)
truth_sources: platform.runs (state, phase, revision, finished_at, output_artifact_id, error_code)
platform.jobs (state, current_attempt_token) and platform.run_attempts (reported_result, exited_at, revoked_at)
object directory: sealed output artifact bytes + sha256
cmd/supervisor exec stdout JSON report; node results via the owner read
independent Decimal truth computed by the test from the input CSV bytes
assertions: result-first: submitWorkerResult is only a proposal — the Run stays state=running, phase=finalizing, unfinished; the job stays leased, the attempt records the result and the execution slot is still allocated

result-first: confirmAttemptExit commits the terminal Run exactly once (revision 3, succeeded, idle, finished_at set, output artifact linked), completes the job, stamps exited_at+revoked_at on the attempt, releases the single quota allocation and keeps exactly the input+output artifact links; the owner read and the artifact content agree
result-first boundaries: a repeated identical exit is idempotent (Run unchanged), a late result is 409 run_terminal, and different exit evidence is 409 attempt_evidence_conflict with no state change
exit-first: confirmAttemptExit alone parks the Run in recovery_pending (phase=idle, no finished_at, revision 3), holds the job instead of completing it, and releases the execution slot
exit-first: the later submitWorkerResult commits the same terminal Run once (revision 4, succeeded, output artifact), completes the held job and keeps exactly one released allocation
exit-first boundaries: a repeated identical exit is idempotent and a late result is 409 run_terminal; neither changes the committed Run

roles: only a worker certificate may submit a result and only a supervisor certificate may confirm exit (maintenance is 403 on both); the needs_reconciliation proposal needs the exit to commit, then stays non-terminal (no finished_at) and a late proposal is 409 run_state_conflict
a result carrying another attempt's token is 409 stale_attempt and stores nothing on either attempt

real executor: `cmd/supervisor exec --once` claims and runs start->python->end in WSL2/runsc; the Run is succeeded with one attempt carrying exited_at+revoked_at, the job is completed, four node results are owner-readable, and the product's Decimal summary equals this test's independently computed decimals from the input bytes

variants.evidence: run 84496ced-5353-4f2c-bfe8-8c004dba544e: outcome=succeeded, attempt exited+revoked, sandbox cleanup={'sandbox_list_matches': 0, 'pid': 822, 'pid_alive': False, 'ps_matches': 0, 'workspace_removed': True}

journeys.title: 后台任务：领取 → 心跳 → 结果（真实 tool_run 处理器 + 内部协议）
entry_commands: cmd/maintenance run --once --kinds tool_run,artifact_finalize (real compiled binary, two real pools; the preset tool runs as a real Python subprocess)
entry_http: GET /api/v1/background-jobs/{job_id} (contract read of the same job)
POST /internal/v1/background/jobs/claim (maintenance mTLS certificate; worker/supervisor certificates are refused)
POST /internal/v1/background/jobs/{job_id}/result (retryable failure -> retry; terminal business failure; duplicate event; different event)
truth_sources: platform.background_jobs (kind, state, attempt_count, lease_token, worker_id, result_event_id, failure_class, error_code, finished_at, available_at)
object directory: sealed summary bytes (sha256) and their Decimal facts
independent Decimal truth computed by the test from the input CSV bytes
cmd/maintenance stdout JSON job reports and exit code
assertions: POST /api/v1/tool-runs (owner + CSRF + Idempotency-Key) returns 202 {id, state, tool, artifact_id}; PostgreSQL holds a ready tool_run job with attempt_count 0
the same Idempotency-Key replays the identical 202 body and creates exactly one job
the real `cmd/maintenance run --once --kinds tool_run,artifact_finalize` claims the job, executes the preset tool and completes it with result=succeeded

independent truth: the job row is succeeded with attempt_count 1, a result_event_id, a finished_at and no error; the job owns ready tool_summary/tool_artifact links; the sealed summary bytes hash to the artifact row and their Decimal total/regions/count equal this test's own Decimal computation from the input CSV (250.00 total, 3 orders); the content route returns the same document; one idempotency receipt was recorded

public boundaries: another creator (and an admin) get 404 for the job and its summary artifact content; a missing Idempotency-Key is 400; the same key with a different body is 409 idempotency_conflict; an unknown tool is 422 with details.field=tool — no job created
claimBackgroundJob rejects worker and supervisor client certificates with 403 forbidden (only the maintenance capacity may claim background work)
claimBackgroundJob (maintenance certificate) returns the real lease and PostgreSQL shows state=leased, attempt_count=1, lease_token=attempt_token and the claiming worker id
a second claim for the same kind is 204: the leased job cannot be taken twice
heartbeatBackgroundJob returns {id, state:leased} and the database lease_deadline moves forward while the token and state stay unchanged

retry/recovery boundary: a retryable infrastructure result (tool_timeout) returns the job to ready with failure_class=infrastructure, attempt_count 1, no result event, no finish, and the old attempt token is refused with 409 stale_attempt on result and heartbeat
the retried job is claimable again after its backoff: a second claim returns a new attempt token and attempt_count=2, and the new token can heartbeat

completeBackgroundJob commits the terminal business result: state=failed, failure_class=business, attempt_count=2, result_event_id/finished_at set, lease cleared, no third attempt, and the public GET /tool-runs/{id} shows the same state/error_code

duplicate delivery is safe: the identical terminal event replays 200 without changing the row; a different event after the terminal result is 409 event_conflict; no further claim is possible for the finished job

known_gaps.title: 聊天正文作为已发布 Run 输入（F08↔F04B 产品缺口）
entry_http: POST /api/v1/requests {message: '把这份销售明细汇总成报告', application_version_id: <published version>} (202 dispatched)
truth_sources: platform.requests + artifacts (the sealed request_input bytes equal the message)
object directory: the Run's input artifact bytes
known_gaps.reason: The Request path seals the chat message verbatim as the Run input (internal/requests/submit.go:131,646-690) while the executor requires a JSON object (internal/presetexec/linear.go:177-187 / graphrun.go:929-937), so the real execution fails with node_input_invalid before any sandbox starts. This is the known F08<->F04B integration gap, not a test-authoring shortcut; the ticket's structured entry (explicit application_version_id + JSON task document) is the in-spec alternative and was not used to claim this chat-text capability.
